walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Networks — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Networks brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Networks.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In a star topology, all devices are connected to:
options: A central switch or hub
Each other in a ring
A single shared cable
The nearest printer

mcqs.q: A phone connected to wireless earbuds over Bluetooth forms a:
options: PAN
WAN
MAN
VPN

mcqs.q: A WAN is best described as:
options: A network connecting computers or LANs across a large geographical area
A network within a single room only
A network with no cables anywhere
Two computers sharing one screen

mcqs.q: Compared with HTTP, HTTPS additionally provides:
options: Encryption of the data exchanged with the website
Faster downloads in all cases
Free web hosting
Protection from power cuts

mcqs.q: Are the internet and the World Wide Web the same thing?
options: No - the internet is the global physical network of networks; the web is one service running on it, alongside email, gaming and video calls.
Yes - cables slow signals down because of friction.
Yes - turning off websites would turn off the internet.
Yes - internet and web are two words for the same system.

mcqs.q: Is a wireless connection always faster than a wired one?
options: Yes - cables slow signals down because of friction.
Yes - star networks shut down for safety whenever a device leaves.
Yes - Wi-Fi is newer technology, so it must be faster.
No - cabled connections are generally faster and more reliable; wireless trades speed and stability for convenience and mobility.

mcqs.q: If one computer in a star network fails, does the whole network go down?
options: Yes - star networks shut down for safety whenever a device leaves.
Yes - any single failure brings down every device in a star network.
Yes - cables slow signals down because of friction.
No - only that device is affected; the network fails as a whole only if the CENTRAL switch or hub fails, which is the topology's weak point.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Network protocol”?
options: A small unit of data sent across a network, carrying a header with addressing and sequencing information as well as the payload itself.
A personal area network connecting devices over a very short range around one person, for example a phone and earbuds linked by Bluetooth.
A network layout in which every device connects to a central switch or hub; a device failure is isolated, but the centre is a single point of failure.
An agreed set of rules for communication, such as HTTP for web pages, SMTP for sending email and TCP/IP for transporting packets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Star topology”?
options: A small unit of data sent across a network, carrying a header with addressing and sequencing information as well as the payload itself.
A local area network covering a small geographical area, such as one building, usually owned and maintained by a single organisation.
A wide area network connecting computers or LANs across large geographical distances, often using third-party infrastructure; the internet is the largest WAN.
A network layout in which every device connects to a central switch or hub; a device failure is isolated, but the centre is a single point of failure.
